title: How to Prevent Scratches on New Hardwood Floors
meta: Prevent scratches on new hardwood with entry mats, felt pads, trimmed pet nails and the right finish sheen. Wills Flooring shares what works in Lynnwood.
keywords: how to prevent scratches on hardwood floors, protect new hardwood floors, hardwood floor scratch protection, felt pads hardwood floors, hardwood floors Lynnwood
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Most scratches on new hardwood come from grit carried in on shoes, so the first defense is a mat outside and a mat inside every door. After that: felt under every furniture leg, trimmed pet nails, no rolling chairs without a mat, and a matte finish that hides the scratches you get anyway.
blocks.detail: You cannot make a hardwood floor scratch-proof. You can make the first five years nearly invisible, and you can pick a wood, finish and sheen at install time that turns a scratch into something only you notice.

blocks.html: We install hardwood in Lynnwood ramblers and split-levels from Alderwood to Martha Lake every week, and the same call comes a month later: a scratch appeared and the homeowner wants to know if the floor is defective. It almost never is. The scratch came from a chair, a dog, or the gravel from a Meadowdale driveway stuck in a boot. This post is what we tell people on that call, plus the decisions before install that matter more than anything after.

blocks.text: Where the scratches actually come from

items.title: Grit at the door
items.text: Sand, gravel and road grit act like sandpaper under shoes. The front entry and the garage door into the kitchen are where most Lynnwood floors show wear first. Two mats per door, one outside and one inside, stop the majority of it.

items.title: Furniture that moves
items.text: Dining chairs pulled out forty times a day, a bar stool, the couch pushed back to vacuum. Every one of those without felt is a scratch. Metal glides and plastic sliders are worse than bare wood legs.

items.title: Dogs, especially big ones
items.text: Nails on a dog over 50 lb will scratch any finish when the dog turns fast on the floor. Trimmed nails and a rug where the dog greets people cut this by most of the total.

items.title: Moving day
items.text: The worst scratches we ever repair happened the day the furniture came back in. Slide nothing. Lift, or use a moving blanket under heavy pieces.

blocks.text: The first 30 days with a new floor

items.text: Prefinished floors can be walked on right away. Site-finished floors take 24 hours for socks and 72 for furniture; the finish keeps hardening for two to four weeks and scratches easiest during that window.
items.note: No rugs on a site-finished floor for 14 days

items.text: Felt on every leg, including the ones you think never move. Check the pads on the dining chairs every couple of months; they pick up grit and wear through.
items.note: Replace plastic sliders and metal glides with felt

items.text: Coarse scraper mat outside, absorbent mat inside, at the front door and the garage door. In a Lynnwood split-level, the landing at the bottom of the entry stairs is the third spot.
items.note: A shoes-off house cuts scratches more than any product

items.text: Nails trimmed every three to four weeks, a runner in the hallway the dog races down, and a rug under the water bowl.
Vacuum with the beater bar off or a soft-floor head, then a water-based hardwood cleaner on a microfiber mop. No steam mops, no oil soaps, no vinegar.
items.note: Grit left on the floor is what scratches it

blocks.text: Products that do not work, or make it worse

a.title: Actually helps
items: Felt pads, the thick kind that screw or nail on for dining chairs
Rubber-backed rugs with a breathable pad, not a solid rubber mat that traps moisture
A chair mat under any rolling office chair
Soft rubber or polyurethane casters if you must roll
A microfiber dust mop used daily in the entry

b.title: Makes it worse
items: Floor polish or wax on a modern finish, which makes future recoats fail
Vinegar and water, which dulls the finish so scratches show more
Steam mops, which push water into the seams
Stick-on felt from the dollar bin that falls off in a month
Scratch-cover markers and oils that stain the wood around the scratch

blocks.text: When a scratch is not your fault, and when it is time to recoat

items.html: A scratch in the finish only looks white or pale and cannot be felt with a fingernail. Normal wear. A recoat erases hundreds of these at once.
A scratch into the wood catches a fingernail and shows bare wood. From a dragged appliance or a dropped tool. Board-level repair, or it waits for the next full refinish.

Finish peeling or flaking in sheets, not lines, is a finish adhesion problem and is covered by our 1-year workmanship warranty on site-finished floors. Wills Flooring is a Metropolitan Hardwood distributor, and we handle factory-finish claims on prefinished planks too.

Recoat, do not refinish. When the traffic lane from the garage door to the kitchen looks dull and scratched but the wood is intact, a screen and recoat at $1.99 per sq ft resets the floor in a day. A 900 sq ft main floor is 900 × $1.99 = $1,791. Waiting until the finish wears through means a full $3.99 sand instead. Details in how to fix scratches without a full refinish.

blocks.title: Honest limit:
blocks.text: If you have two large dogs and want a dark, smooth, high-gloss floor, no amount of felt will keep it looking new. Either change the spec to a matte, textured, mid-tone oak, or consider vinyl plank in the rooms the dogs use. We will say this at the estimate rather than sell you a floor you will be unhappy with.
Scratch-prevention checklist for a new Lynnwood floor

items.html: Two mats at every exterior door before the furniture comes back.
Felt on every leg, checked and replaced twice a year.
Nail trims on a schedule and a runner in the dog's racing lane.
Dust mop the entries daily, damp mop weekly with a water-based hardwood cleaner only.
Choose matte or satin, mid-tone, and some texture at the sample stage. See our hardwood installation page for what we bring to the house.
Book a recoat at year four or five, before the finish wears through in the traffic lane. It is the cheapest floor maintenance you will ever pay for.

faq.q: Do felt pads really prevent scratches on hardwood?
faq.a: Yes, as long as they are clean and attached. The thick nail-on or screw-on pads last years on dining chairs; thin stick-on pads fall off within months. Check them when you vacuum, because a felt pad with grit embedded in it scratches like sandpaper.

faq.q: What is the most scratch-resistant hardwood floor?
faq.a: A hard species like white oak or hickory, in a wire-brushed texture, with a matte factory finish and a natural or mid-brown color. That combination resists scratches and hides the ones it gets. Wills Flooring installs it at $3.25 per sq ft labor plus material.

faq.q: Are dog nails bad for hardwood floors?
faq.a: Untrimmed nails on a large dog will scratch any finish, especially when the dog turns fast on a smooth floor. Trimmed nails, a runner in the hallway and a rug at the door handle most of it. A matte, textured oak hides the rest.

faq.q: Can rolling office chairs go on hardwood?
faq.a: With a chair mat, yes. Without one, standard hard plastic casters grind grit into the finish in a small circle under the desk. Soft polyurethane casters help but a mat is the reliable answer. Check that the mat itself is smooth underneath, because a cracked or gritty mat scratches too.

faq.q: How do I get rid of light scratches on new hardwood floors?
faq.a: Scratches in the finish only are removed by a screen and recoat, which abrades the top layer and applies a fresh coat. Wills Flooring charges $1.99 per sq ft with a 500 sq ft minimum. Do not use scratch-cover oils or markers; they stain the wood and make a future recoat fail.

faq.q: Do area rugs damage hardwood floors?
faq.a: Only if the backing is solid rubber or PVC, which traps moisture and can discolor the finish, or if the rug goes down on a site-finished floor before the finish has cured. Use a breathable felt or felt-and-rubber rug pad and wait two weeks after a site finish.
